messages:
sophia (CS): hey team, getting an escalation from a power-user — multiple calls to /v1/generate returning 502/504 since ~10:24. They said errors spiked right after the canary went out. Ticket #INC-5234. Can someone triage? :warning:

maria (SRE): on it. any useful identifiers from the customer? region, model id, route?

sophia (CS): region: us-west1, model: open-redwood-13b, route: text.generate.default. They attached a curl sample and logs showing gateway 502s + long upstream timeouts.

kevin (Runtime): I see a canary for the new routing flag rolled at 10:22 by deploy-bot. rolling 10% -> 50% -> 100? Let me pull the config.

deploy-bot: deploy started by @ben at 2026-03-15T10:21:34Z — canary: routing-v2, config flag: use_kv_prefetch=true, percentage: 10% -> 100% (auto-promote enabled).

ben (Eng): ugh I merged the change this morning. auto-promote was left on accidentally. I thought we were landing only the health checks.

maria (SRE): correlation: 5xx rate for text.generate.default in us-west1 jumped from ~0.2% to 8.7% at 10:24. latency p50 -> p95 increased. link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/requests?panel=5xx&region=us-west1

oncall: can we toggle traffic back to last stable? I can apply route-override to send all traffic to routing-v1.

kevin (Runtime): before we flip, quick hypothesis: use_kv_prefetch changes runtime memory access pattern for KV cache which on certain GPU kernels causes timeouts under bursty short-seq workloads. I have a repro script.

maria (SRE): we need mitigation now — confirm rollback plan. Options:
- flip route override to routing-v1 (fast, zero deploy)
- flip the flag off at config store (but propagation ~30s-2m)
- scale up dedicated pool (temporary)
Which do we want?

ben (Eng): route override please. I'll also open a PR to disable auto-promote and add a safety guard.

devex: Sophia, could you ask the customer to send the exact request/headers (they had a custom x-client-id) so we can match traces? Also notify them we're working on a rollback.

maria (SRE): oncall — apply override now.

oncall: applying route override -> all text.generate.default in us-west1 -> routing-v1.

oncall: done. propagation started.

maria (SRE): metrics: 5xx rate dropping, now 1.2% at 10:29. p95 latency decreasing. keep watching for the next 5m.

kevin (Runtime): confirmed from logs: the canary variant started returning repeated streaming handshake failures with 502s due to handshake timeouts on the kernel path. stack traces point to prefetch code path. Repro script attached below:
```
# repro simple loop against canary
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"open-redwood-13b","input":"hi","max_tokens":10}' || echo "ERR $i"
  sleep 0.2
done
```

ben (Eng): can we cut the canary variant image and run it in staging with the prefetch turned on + heavy short-seq traffic to confirm? I'll queue that.

maria (SRE): for public postmortem checklist: preserve logs for 10:20-10:35, snapshots of routing configs, deploy history, customer traces. Sophia — pass ETA to customer: we've routed them off the canary, and errors should be resolved. Ask them to confirm.

sophia (CS): told them we've applied a route override and engineers are digging in. Customer reports API is back to normal for their workload. Thanks team. :heart:

kevin (Runtime): follow-up tasks assigned: 1) revert auto-promote default or add a manual gate (PR open) 2) add unit test for prefetch hot-path on short-seq workloads 3) add a canary healthcheck that simulates burst short sequences (ticket RT-881).

maria (SRE): leaving this thread open until we have a rollback PR or mitigation deployed. Also flag support billing team: customer saw elevated request retries during the window, may affect billing credits. @sophia (CS) please coordinate.

sophia (CS): will loop in billing. cc: @devex for any docs we should update about canary auto-promote.

ben (Eng): PR to disable auto-promote: https://stash.redwood.dev/pull/3491 — awaiting review.

maria (SRE): closing notes: root cause likely mis-scoped config (auto-promote) + unchecked runtime prefetch code path under bursty short-sequence traffic. Immediate mitigation: route override; medium: disable auto-promote + add test; long: runtime fix and safer rollout gating. Will draft incident postmortem after full logs and traces.

deploy-bot: ticket INC-5234 -> incident created and linked to PR 3491.
